cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Assigned by Procedure
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept an unwanted responsibility by proving that the rules, rotation, or tradition make it theirs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Congratulations on becoming club president. Here are the toilet keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought the caretaker cleaned them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We voted to save that fee. The minutes assign closing and cleaning to the president.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I proposed that when you were president.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, and I cleaned them all year. Your first presidential duty is continuing your savings.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs new president to toilet keys; A3 invokes voted minutes over B assumption; A5 defines B first presidential duty, enacting higher status even after leaving the office.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 caretaker assumption causes A3 fee-saving rule; B4 authorship admission causes A5 continuity of the savings B imposed on A.

relationship.evidence: B2 expects paid cleaning and B4 acknowledges proposing the rule under A, making the obligation personal and intelligible.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 admission to assign continuation of B own savings, a specific reversal of position rather than an arbitrary duty.

specificity.evidence: A1 club presidency and toilet keys, A3 minutes and A5 year of cleaning establish duties clearly.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 old generic preface remains expendable; A5 your savings is earned by B4 own proposal.
